description:
One-click accept of a **held** decision (accountant) — posts the AI's proposal.

The accepting actor's approval replaces every soft guardrail (confidence,
amount cap, risk flags); hard blocks stay enforced by the posting path (closed
period / sealed FY / unresolvable accounts → 409/422). The accepted entry posts
as ``origin=ai`` with the accepting user in the audit trail
(``accepted_by``/``accepted_at`` + JE ``posted_by``); the row flips
``held → posted`` in place, so a second accept is a 409 (idempotent).

``accepted_by_kind`` records what kind of actor approved: an accept made over
MCP is recorded as ``mcp``, not as a person's click.

The optional ``body`` serves three holds (and two confirmations only a person in
the app may send) and is omitted for every other kind:
``expense:receipt:item:`` needs ``employee_id`` + ``category_id`` for the draft
claim, ``autopost:capitalize:`` needs ``fixed_asset_category_id`` (+ optional
``useful_life_months``) when the hold resolved no category, and a
``needs_split_source`` mixed invoice needs ``reclassify_from_account_code`` —
422 without them.

anyOf.description:
Optional ``POST /autopost-decisions/{id}/accept`` body.

Two paths read it. The ``expense:receipt:item:`` claim path needs an employee
and a category (both NOT NULL on the claim plane). The ``autopost:capitalize:``
path needs a ``fixed_asset_category_id`` when the hold could not resolve one —
a missing category is a 422, never a guess, because the wrong category posts
the cost to the wrong balance-sheet account and depreciates it into the wrong
expense. The capitalize path may need a third fact:
``reclassify_from_account_code`` when the hold is a mixed-invoice split whose
source line did not resolve (``needs_split_source``) — again a 422 without it,
never a guess. Omit the body entirely for every other decision kind (backward
compatible).

name: accept_autopost_decision
